title: Stacks: Valid Parentheses
oneLiner: Push on every open bracket, pop-and-match on every close -- the stack tells you if anything's out of order.
keyTakeaway: A stack is LIFO -- last in, first out. Reach for one whenever a problem is about matching or nesting (brackets, undo history, DFS backtracking): the most recently opened thing has to be the first thing closed, which is exactly what push/pop gives you for free.
explanation: A stack only supports two moves -- push (add to the top) and pop (remove from the top) -- and that's exactly the shape "is this bracket string balanced" needs. Walk the string; on every open bracket, push it. On every close bracket, pop the top and check it's the matching open -- if the stack is empty (nothing to pop) or the popped bracket doesn't match, the string is invalid immediately. At the very end, the stack must be empty too -- an unclosed open bracket (like "(") passes every per-character check but still isn't valid. Watch out for both failure directions: popping an empty stack (too many closes) and a non-empty stack at the end (too many opens) are two separate bugs people forget to check.

visualizationSteps.message: Walk "{[()]}" left to right. Empty stack to start.
'{' is an open bracket -- push it. Stack: [{]
'[' is an open bracket -- push it. Stack: [{ []
'(' is an open bracket -- push it. Stack: [{ [ (]
')' matches the top of the stack ('(') -- pop it. Stack: [{ []
']' matches the top of the stack ('[') -- pop it. Stack: [{]
'}' matches the top of the stack ('{') -- pop it. Stack: []
Every open was matched and the stack is empty at the end -- valid.

complexity.note: Each character is pushed and popped at most once; in the worst case (all openers) the stack holds n items.
